previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with a history of kidney transplant, coronary artery disease, and multiple comorbidities, was admitted for acute volume overload with 14 pounds of weight gain and lower extremity edema, along with a painful right leg hematoma after trauma. She was treated with IV furosemide, achieving a net negative fluid balance of 2.1 liters. Her kidney function temporarily worsened, with creatinine rising to 1.9, but improved to 1.8 by discharge. Heart function remained stable with LVEF of 51%, and transplant ultrasound was normal. Pain from the leg contusion was managed with hydromorphone, and she was discharged home with instructions to hold diuretics for two days, restart at a lower dose, and follow up for lab monitoring. Immunosuppressant levels were therapeutic, and all chronic medications were continued.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year-old female with past medical history of FSGN status post 
living-unrelated renal transplant in ___, Coronary Artery 
Disease with NSTEMI, lacunar strokes, osteonecrosis of the long 
bones, and recent diagnosis of congestive heart failure ___ 
who presented with right flank (actually right lumbar/sacral) 
pain, right lower quadrant pain over transplanted kidney, 
nausea, and diarrhea over 5 days, as well as recent 15lb weight 
gain between ___ after stopping furosemide (though weight 
was downtrending on arrival having restarted furosemide).

#FLANK/ABDOMINAL PAIN/DIARRHEA: Unclear etiology. Concerning for 
rejection. Her native kidneys are atrophic and are unlikely to 
have stones; further, no stones seen on CTU. No dysuria and UA 
unremarkable, reassuring for no UTI and culture with mixed flora 
(contaminant). Could be gastroenteritis in setting of diarrhea 
(patient has chronic diarrhea for ___ days and then no stool for 
___ days, so 5 straight days of diarrhea atypical); however, 
diarrhea resolved by admission and no stool samples were thus 
able to be sent. Of note, she does have history of C.diff, but 
her picture was never concerning for evolution to toxic 
megacolon. Differential is broadened in immunosuppression; CMV 
and BK virus pending. CTU did not show diverticulitis. Biliary 
pathology less likely given normal LFTs; mildly elevated lipase 
in ED resolved by ___. Other etiologies include renal 
transplant rejection (see below). Pain controlled with standing 
1g TID acetaminophen and PO dilaudid; patient takes vicodin at 
home.

#ACUTE KIDNEY INJURY: Creatinine improved from 2.7 on admission 
to 1.8 (same as 3 days prior to admission) ___ apparently 
prerenal from volume losses (gastroenteritis, nausea), supported 
by UNa <20. Injury may have had component of restarting 
furosemide, having put on reported 15lb when she held it. 
Transplant rejection cannot be excluded especially given 
tenderness of transplant location. Somewhat reassuring that 
ultrasound is normal. Will be discharged on half normal dose of 
furosemide with plan to follow up within 14 days, and have 
repeat labs by ___, including Chem 7 and tacro/sirolimus.
